extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans and researchers seeking a biography/profile of a stand-up comedian
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style biographical profile of a stand-up comedian covering early life, career, style, controversies, broadcasts, and awards. Useful for understanding a comedian's style, reputation, and public incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres / comedic subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres: Social satire, observational comedy; Subjects: Society, culture, human interaction, racism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the show's topical focus and tone: social satire and observational comedy suggest material aimed at societal issues and human behaviour, including sensitive topics like racism. Use these labels to judge expected content and audience fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of provocative racial language in show titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Hunter often uses variations of the term "nigga" in the titles of his shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include 'Reginald D Hunter: Pride & Prejudice... & Niggas' (poster banned from the London Underground) and the 'Trophy Nigga' tour (not all venues used the tour title). This practice is a branding/edginess strategy but has clear promotional and reputational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary-pushing / offensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: "still not for the faint-hearted and easily offended"; performer statement: "as a comedian, I do push boundaries in creating humour".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comedian explicitly adopts an approach that pushes boundaries; expect material that may be "highly offensive" to some. Usefulness as a criterion: measure how deliberately provocative the material is and how that aligns with artistic intent or audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic breadth and concise skewering
rubrics_metrics.description: "moves elegantly from big topic to big topic, concisely skewering each subject".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive critical metric: ability to cover large themes succinctly and sharply. Reviewers cite this as a sign of craft and versatility; evaluate sets on topical range and the economy/precision of the punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reaction and controversy as an evaluative signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of audience members objecting, booing, leaving; reviewers noting material as "highly offensive"; organisations criticising jokes (e.g., Campaign Against Antisemitism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience behaviour (booing, leaving, applause) and public controversy are important indicators of how material lands outside critics. They can signal whether material is perceived as crossing social boundaries, and may impact bookings and public image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue/promoter sensitivity and censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoters/venues sometimes avoid using controversial tour titles; posters banned from public transport (London Underground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing and presentation may be modified by third parties for sensitivity reasons. When evaluating or planning shows, consider how venue or promoter risk-aversion will affect title usage, posters, and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and reputational risk from public statements and social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Private prosecution alleging offences under section 127 of the Communications Act 2003 relating to posts allegedly published on X; police concluded "no crime was established"; judge later quashed summons and criticised the prosecuting organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic material and public posts can create legal exposure and reputational consequences. Track outcomes (charges, prosecutions, quashed summonses) and note that legal resolution (e.g., 'no crime established') is a separate measure from public outrage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception, awards, and broadcasting credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominated for the Perrier Award (2003, 2004); won the Writers' Guild Award for Comedy in 2006; numerous BBC Radio and television appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry recognition (nominations, awards) and frequent broadcast/TV credits are standard metrics of professional success and peer recognition. Use these to assess stature and quality in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career longevity and festival/tour activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Years active: 1992–present; tours (e.g., 2013 Ireland tour), Edinburgh Fringe performances, podcast hosting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longevity, festival appearances (Edinburgh Fringe), and tour history signal sustained relevance and professional development. Evaluate a comedian by years active, festival participation, and the scale/frequency of tours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accumulated contentious history as context for new incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Past controversial jokes (including references to the Holocaust) are cited when new incidents occur (e.g., later CAA criticism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A performer’s prior history of controversial material influences how future jokes are interpreted and criticized. When assessing an incident, consider prior incidents and how they form patterns that affect public and institutional reactions.
